claims.text: Adding a minor amount of aluminum to an elemental Cr coating on zirconium-alloy cladding will improve coating durability.
Aluminum addition will promote formation of protective Cr–Al oxide phases at the coating surface.
Aluminum addition will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The modified coating will provide better performance than pure Cr in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
The Cr–Al oxide surface layer will act as a diffusion barrier.
The Cr–Al oxide surface layer will improve adherence between the coating and zirconium-alloy cladding.
Mixed Cr–Al oxide phases are more resistant to oxidation than the oxide scale produced by an elemental Cr coating.
Mixed Cr–Al oxide phases are more resistant to interfacial diffusion.
Suppressing high-temperature interdiffusion will prevent premature coating failure and preserve coating integrity.
The aluminum-alloyed coating will have a lower oxidation rate than an elemental Cr coating.
The aluminum-alloyed coating will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than an elemental Cr coating.
Unmodified elemental Cr coatings fail to provide adequate performance across both water and steam regimes because of elevated-temperature interdiffusion.
The intervention is expected to be effective at approximately 300°C in subcritical water.
The intervention is expected to be effective in steam at temperatures up to approximately 1200°C.
